title: Container Apps vs AKS
description: Compare Azure Container Apps and AKS to understand when to use each platform for containerized workloads.

data.text: Both Container Apps and AKS run containers on Azure, but they serve different audiences. Container Apps abstracts Kubernetes entirely, while AKS exposes the full Kubernetes API.

cards.title: Container Apps
cards.description: Serverless container platform built on Kubernetes.

cards.title: AKS
cards.description: Managed Kubernetes cluster with full API access.

rows: Scale to zero to save costs

data.title: Start with Container Apps
data.text: If you are unsure, start with Container Apps. It offers the simplest path to production. You can migrate to AKS later if you need deeper Kubernetes control.

data.caption: Decision tree for choosing a container platform
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    Q1{Need Kubernetes API?} -->|No| CA[Container Apps]
    Q1 -->|Yes| Q2{Have K8s expertise?}
    Q2 -->|Yes| AKS[AKS]
    Q2 -->|No| Q3{Can you learn K8s?}
    Q3 -->|Yes| AKS
    Q3 -->|No| CA

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Container Apps: serverless, abstracts Kubernetes, simpler
AKS: full Kubernetes control, more operational responsibility
Choose Container Apps for simplicity and cost savings
Choose AKS for full Kubernetes feature access
data.takeaway: Pick the platform that matches your team's expertise and operational needs.
